classification: Local maintained regression evidence; no provider sends, cloud run, monthly cost qualification or shipment claim
rootCause: TSX evaluates the ESM package clock through separate static CommonJS and dynamic ESM module instances. Per-module UUID generation assigns different identities even though both samplers use the same runtime performance.now domain. The recorder consequently refuses gateway attempts as foreign-clock before fetch.
alternativeHypothesis: The recorder and gateway run in separate processes and legitimately need distinct clock domains.
distinguishingTest: The maintained Vitest test captures exact clock source bytes in a temporary type:module fixture, launches the real installed TSX loader with inherited source guards, and imports the fixture statically and dynamically within one child. A second case compares separately launched processes. Child-computed source SHA256 must match the captured source.

predictions.rootCause: Within one TSX child the original module yields different objects; a process-global singleton makes them equal while separate children remain distinct.
predictions.alternativeHypothesis: Within-process objects would already agree before the change; a subprocess is required to observe identity divergence.

before.failure: sameObject was false inside one TSX process

after.testedNamedPathProvenance: 1 of 2 named test paths dirty; production clock source captured directly by child fixture
coverage: Static CommonJS and dynamic ESM imports share immutable object and id
Separately launched processes retain distinct clock ids
Foreign clock attempt remains denied before reservation

Full write-ahead reservations cover concurrency, retries and response outcomes
after.postTestChange: Production JSDoc clarified runtime-global semantics only; executable source unchanged after the successful run
